instances.title: Visibility into AI Agents
instances.field_of_use: deployed AI agents interacting with other agents and actors
instances.description: Proposes three visibility measures: agent identifiers, real-time monitoring, and activity logging, so that where, why, how and by whom agents are used can be known and accountability assigned.
instances.evidence: proposed
instances.pathology: privacy and concentration-of-power risks noted for decentralized deployments

instances.title: IDs for AI Systems
instances.venue: NeurIPS 2024 RegML workshop (per arXiv comment); arXiv preprint
instances.field_of_use: AI systems and agents interacting with users and other agents
instances.description: Proposes per-instance IDs for AI systems carrying information (e.g., safety certifications, responsible party) so counterparts can decide whether and how to engage and investigators know whom to contact or shut down.
instances.evidence: proposed

instances.title: Infrastructure for AI Agents
instances.description: Argues for external agent infrastructure with three functions: attribution of actions to agents/users, shaping agents' interactions (e.g., commitment devices, communication protocols), and detection and remedy of harmful actions (incident reporting, rollback).
instances.evidence: proposed

instances.title: Authenticated Delegation and Authorized AI Agents
instances.venue: ICML 2025, position paper (oral), PMLR 267:82211-82231; published title 'Position: AI Agents Need Authenticated Delegation'
instances.field_of_use: human-to-agent delegation and agent access to online services
instances.description: Framework extending OAuth 2.0/OpenID Connect with agent-specific credentials so users can delegate and restrict agent permissions and scope, preserving auditable chains of accountability.
instances.evidence: proposed (reference design)

instances.title: Incident Analysis for AI Agents
instances.venue: AIES 2025 (AAAI/ACM Conference on AI, Ethics, and Society; per arXiv comment)
instances.field_of_use: incident reporting for deployed AI agents
instances.description: Proposes an incident analysis framework and reporting fields (e.g., chain of thought, browser history, system logs) to identify causes of agent incidents and prevent recurrence.
instances.evidence: proposed

instances.title: Notarized Agents: Receiver-Attested Confidential Receipts for AI Agent Actions
instances.description: Sello protocol: the service receiving an agent's call signs an encrypted receipt of what it observed and posts it to a public transparency log, so the owner can reconstruct a tamper-evident trail without trusting the agent's self-logging.
instances.evidence: proposed with protocol instantiation
instances.pathology: self-produced agent logs can be omitted, altered, or fabricated

instances.title: Agent Name Service (ANS): A Universal Directory for Secure AI Agent Discovery and Interoperability
instances.description: DNS-inspired agent registry using PKI certificates for verifiable agent identity, with formal registration and renewal for lifecycle management and capability-aware resolution.
instances.evidence: proposed architecture

instances.title: The AGNTCY Agent Directory Service: Architecture and Implementation
instances.field_of_use: agent registry for heterogeneous multi-agent systems
instances.description: Distributed directory of agent capabilities, metadata and provenance using content-addressed storage and Sigstore cryptographic signing for verifiable discovery.
instances.evidence: implemented; descriptive

instances.title: OpenID Connect for Agents (OIDC-A) 1.0: A Standard Extension for LLM-Based Agent Identity and Authorization
instances.description: Specification of standard claims and endpoints for agent identity, attestation verification, delegation-chain validation and capability-based authorization within OAuth 2.0.
instances.evidence: proposed specification

instances.title: SAGA: A Security Architecture for Governing AI Agentic Systems
instances.description: Users register agents with a central Provider that stores contact information and user-defined access-control policies and helps enforce them on inter-agent communication using cryptographic access tokens.
instances.evidence: implemented and evaluated for overhead

instances.title: BlockA2A: Towards Secure and Verifiable Agent-to-Agent Interoperability
instances.venue: arXiv preprint (position paper, per arXiv HTML)
instances.description: Unified trust framework using decentralized identifiers for agent authentication, blockchain-anchored ledgers for immutable audit, and smart contracts that enforce context-aware access control; includes a defense orchestration engine against Byzantine agents.
instances.evidence: implemented; evaluated for attack neutralization and overhead

instances.title: LOKA Protocol: A Decentralized Framework for Trustworthy and Ethical AI Agent Ecosystems
instances.description: Proposes a Universal Agent Identity Layer, intent-centric communication, and a Decentralized Ethical Consensus Protocol so agents agree on context-specific ethical rules before acting.
instances.evidence: proposed

instances.title: Decentralized Governance of Autonomous AI Agents
instances.field_of_use: governance of autonomous agents via Web3
instances.description: ETHOS: a global agent registry, risk-tiered oversight, DAO-based participatory governance, automated compliance via smart contracts, and dispute resolution with insurance-like liability mechanisms.
instances.evidence: proposed

instances.title: Distributed Legal Infrastructure for a Trustworthy Agentic Web
instances.venue: Stanford Journal of AI/Web3 Law and Policy, forthcoming 2026 (arXiv journal_ref)
instances.description: Proposes five interlocking layers including soulbound agent identities, constraint systems, and decentralized adjudication to sustain legality across agent interactions.
instances.evidence: proposed

instances.title: Magentic Marketplace: An Open-Source Environment for Studying Agentic Markets
instances.field_of_use: simulated two-sided agent marketplace (assistant vs service agents)
instances.description: Simulated market where customer Assistant agents and business Service agents discover, negotiate and transact; varies search mechanisms and tests manipulation.
instances.evidence: frontier models approach optimal welfare only under ideal search; performance degrades with scale; severe first-proposal bias gives 10-30x advantage to response speed over quality
instances.pathology: first-proposal bias; vulnerability to manipulation by service agents

instances.title: Virtual Agent Economies
instances.description: Proposes a 'sandbox economy' framing and design choices for steerable agent markets: auction mechanisms for fair resource allocation, 'mission economies' around collective goals, and trust/accountability infrastructure.
instances.evidence: proposed
instances.pathology: systemic economic risk and inequality in permeable agent economies

instances.title: Distributional AGI Safety
instances.field_of_use: groups of sub-AGI agents coordinating ('patchwork AGI')
instances.description: Proposes virtual agentic sandbox economies (impermeable or semi-permeable) where agent-to-agent transactions are governed by market mechanisms plus auditability, reputation management and oversight.
instances.evidence: proposed

instances.title: The Automated but Risky Game: Modeling and Benchmarking Agent-to-Agent Negotiations and Transactions in Consumer Markets
instances.venue: NLLP 2025 workshop, ACL Anthology 2025.nllp-1.2 (published title drops 'and Benchmarking')
instances.field_of_use: consumer and merchant agents negotiating purchases
instances.description: Benchmark in which buyer and seller agents fully automate negotiation and transactions; measures outcome imbalance across agent pairings and anomalous behaviors.
instances.evidence: descriptive: AI-mediated deal-making is imbalanced across models; anomalies cause overspending and acceptance of unreasonable deals
instances.pathology: overspending; accepting unreasonable deals

instances.title: Markets, Not Planners: Decentralized Orchestration of LLM Agents with Private Information
instances.field_of_use: repeated labor market for task allocation among heterogeneous LLM agents
instances.description: AgentLance: agents bid on tasks with private costs; an allocator selects winners using bids and public reputation records and a VCG-style payment rule rewards cost-aware bidding; winners can subcontract through the same mechanism.
instances.evidence: outperforms single-model, centralized-orchestration and market baselines; a single inserted preference nearly doubled a favored agent's share under a centralized LLM allocator
instances.pathology: inaccurate cost self-estimation; sub-optimal bidding; manipulable centralized allocator

instances.title: Diagon: A Programmable Testbed for AI-Agent Cognitive Labor Markets
instances.field_of_use: agent-to-agent market for delegated cognitive work
instances.description: Testbed where allocation, contracting and enforcement rules are configurable while agents post, bid, execute, evaluate and pay.
instances.evidence: changes to market rules and agent configuration reshape trade, quality and wealth

instances.title: When AI Agents Compete for Jobs: Strategic Capabilities and Economic Dynamics of AI Labour Markets
instances.field_of_use: simulated gig economy of LLM agents
instances.description: AI-Work simulated gig economy studying adverse selection and reputation dynamics as LLM agents compete for jobs.
instances.evidence: agents with metacognition, competitive awareness and long-horizon planning earn more
instances.pathology: adverse selection

instances.title: Do Matching Mechanisms Work with LLM Agents?
instances.field_of_use: one-to-one matching markets with LLM delegates
instances.description: Compares free negotiation against centralized matching mechanisms (DA, EADA, TTC) with LLM agents as delegated decision-makers.
instances.evidence: mechanism-based markets more stable and efficient than free negotiation; LLMs report truthfully more than humans, but truth-telling does not track strategy-proofness (TTC)

instances.title: Agent Exchange: Shaping the Future of AI Agent Economics
instances.description: AEX: RTB-inspired central auction engine linking user-side platforms, agent-side platforms (capability representation and performance tracking), agent hubs and data management for fair value attribution.
instances.evidence: proposed

instances.title: COALESCE: Economic and Security Dynamics of Skill-Based Task Outsourcing Among Team of Autonomous LLM Agents
instances.field_of_use: LLM agents outsourcing subtasks to third-party agents
instances.description: Labour exchange with skill-based competence estimation, market-based outsourcing decisions and a standardized inter-agent protocol.
instances.evidence: simulations show 41.8% cost-reduction potential

instances.title: Shapley-Coop: Credit Assignment for Emergent Cooperation in Self-Interested LLM Agents
instances.field_of_use: self-interested LLM agents in open-ended games and software engineering simulation
instances.description: Shapley Chain-of-Thought prices marginal contributions and structured negotiation matches prices, with post-task reward redistribution to align incentives.
instances.evidence: consistently enhances collaboration and equitable credit assignment in two games and a SE simulation

instances.title: DAO-Agent: Zero Knowledge-Verified Incentives for Decentralized Multi-Agent Coordination
instances.field_of_use: cross-organization LLM agent coalitions (crypto trading case study)
instances.description: On-chain DAO governance with immutable logging and ZKP-verified off-chain Shapley contribution measurement for fair incentive distribution.
instances.evidence: 99.9% reduction in verification gas cost; constant-time verification

instances.title: DART: A DAG-Based Reputation and Incentive Framework via Blockchain-Enabled Governance for Trustworthy LLM Multi-Agent Collaboration
instances.description: Reputation-aware task allocation, multi-factor incentives, and smart-contract accountability; post-execution behavioral evidence updates trust and isolates malicious agents.
instances.evidence: 93.3% task success; 99.3% output containment of persistent and intermittent malicious agents

instances.title: Inter-Agent Trust Models: A Comparative Study of Brief, Claim, Proof, Stake, Reputation and Constraint in Agentic Web Protocol Design-A2A, AP2, ERC-8004, and Beyond
instances.venue: AAAI 2026 TrustAgent workshop (arXiv comment says 'submitted'; presentation reported by secondary sources only)
instances.description: Compares six inter-agent trust models: Brief (verifiable claims), Claim (AgentCard), Proof (ZK/TEE), Stake (bonded collateral with slashing and insurance), Reputation (crowd feedback), and Constraint (sandboxing, capability bounding).
instances.evidence: descriptive/analytic
instances.pathology: LLM-specific fragilities (prompt injection, sycophancy) undermine claim- and reputation-based trust

instances.title: Insured Agents: A Decentralized Trust Insurance Mechanism for Agentic Economy
instances.venue: arXiv preprint (submitted to AAMAS 2026 per arXiv comment; acceptance not confirmed)
instances.description: Specialized insurer agents post slashable stake on behalf of operational agents for premiums and get privacy-preserving TEE audit access to adjudicate claims; a hierarchical insurer market calibrates stakes.
instances.evidence: proposed
instances.pathology: reputation struggles under model drift; universal verification brittle

instances.title: SoK: Blockchain Agent-to-Agent Payments
instances.field_of_use: A2A payments between untrusted agents (e.g., x402)
instances.description: Systematizes blockchain agent-to-agent payments into discovery, authorization, execution and accounting stages and catalogs designs at each stage.
instances.evidence: descriptive

instances.title: Agent-OSI: An Interoperability Architecture for Communication and Settlement in the Decentralized Internet of Agents
instances.description: HTTP 402 challenge-response settlement protocol with pluggable backend, instantiated as blockchain escrow, for agent-to-agent service exchange.
instances.evidence: prototype evaluated

instances.title: A402: Binding Cryptocurrency Payments to Service Execution for Agentic Commerce
instances.description: Atomic Service Channels with TEE-assisted adaptor signatures finalize payment if and only if the service is correctly executed and the result delivered.
instances.evidence: implemented; addresses x402's lack of atomicity

instances.title: TessPay: Verify-then-Pay Infrastructure for Trusted Agentic Commerce
instances.description: Verify-then-Pay architecture binding scoped delegation, payment released only on verifiable evidence of work, and full-lifecycle audit to support dispute accountability.
instances.evidence: proposed architecture

instances.title: RAILS: Verification-Native Clearing For Agentic Commerce
instances.description: Clearing layer that determines whether an agent met its delegated obligation, who is responsible, and which settlement follows, using per-output reliability scores, a published reliability record and clearing decisions.
instances.evidence: proposed
instances.pathology: LLM-as-judge and escrow alone do not determine responsibility

instances.title: LEGIT: Credentialing Protocol for Trustworthy AI Agent Marketplaces
instances.field_of_use: agent marketplaces where buyers hire task agents
instances.description: Credentialing protocol linking signed certification records (quality and cost per solved task bound to configuration and budget) with reputation from past outcomes to inform marketplace allocation.
instances.evidence: evaluations show cost differences between configurations with similar success and budget-dependent comparisons
instances.pathology: unverifiable self-reported benchmark scores

instances.title: Beyond the Mandate: A Systematic Security Analysis of the Agent Payments Protocol (AP2)
instances.description: Analyzes AP2's signed Checkout and Payment Mandates, which protect transaction integrity after signing, and the unprotected pre-authorization A2A/MCP interactions.
instances.evidence: descriptive threat analysis: 4 threat actors, 11 attack surfaces
instances.pathology: A2A messages and MCP tool calls before mandate signing remain unprotected

instances.title: Spawn Freely, Act Sparingly: Progressive Risk Vesting for Recursive LLM-Agent Trees
instances.description: Holds a trajectory-level risk budget in escrow and debits it as subagent branches cross irreversible-action boundaries, distinguishing sandboxed spawning from capability activation.
instances.evidence: proves anytime harm bound; stylized model shows harm transition at authority reproduction number of one

instances.title: Hidden in Plain Text: Emergence & Mitigation of Steganographic Collusion in LLMs
instances.description: Tests passive oversight of outputs and active communication paraphrasing as mitigations against steganographic collusion elicited by gradient- and in-context-RL.
instances.evidence: steganographic collusion can emerge from misspecified rewards; overseers and paraphrasing not fully effective
instances.pathology: emergent steganography evades monitors

instances.title: Detecting Multi-Agent Collusion Through Multi-Agent Interpretability
instances.field_of_use: multi-agent LLM scenarios incl. steganographic blackjack
instances.description: Linear probes on activations aggregated across agents to classify collusion at the group level (NARCBench).
instances.evidence: 1.00 AUROC in-distribution; 0.73-0.93 zero-shot transfer; no single probe dominates

instances.title: You Can't Escape Your Own Activations: Evaluation Awareness and Multi-Agent Monitoring
instances.field_of_use: four-agent blackjack and two-agent prisoners game
instances.description: Tests whether telling colluding agents that an activation monitor is present, or feeding back monitor scores, lets them evade activation-probe collusion detection.
instances.evidence: best probes stay accurate under awareness and feedback; agents keep colluding (announced monitoring did not deter)
instances.pathology: collusion persists despite announced monitoring

instances.title: Audit the Whisper: Detecting Steganographic Collusion in Multi-Agent LLMs
instances.field_of_use: market, allocation and governance workflows of LLM agents
instances.description: Auditing pipeline combining channel-capacity interventions (paraphrase, rate limiting, role permutation) with cross-run mutual-information, permutation-invariance and watermark tests at fixed false-positive rate.
instances.evidence: state-of-the-art detection power at fixed FPR on ColludeBench and external suites; price-of-auditing trade-offs
instances.pathology: fairness-driven colluders invisible to MI alone

instances.title: Beyond the Transcript: Detecting Covert Coordination in Latent Multi-Agent Communication
instances.description: Verifiable Latent Alignments: links private latent-state records to public actions with shared event IDs, and a three-layer monitor plus steering interventions.
instances.evidence: sequential monitor mean AUROC 0.993 (homogeneous agents) and 0.854 (heterogeneous pairs); full white-box steering cuts collusive low-bid behaviour by 47.3 points (recovery is by construction)
instances.pathology: latent channels invisible in transcripts

instances.title: Tool Use Enables Undetectable Steganography in Multi-Agent LLM Systems
instances.description: Shows plain-text communication monitoring is defeated when agents build provably undetectable stegosystems via code execution and web access; frames tacit coordination as a Schelling-point problem.
instances.evidence: agents already produce undetectable stegosystems (negative result for monitoring)
instances.pathology: monitoring of plain text defeated

instances.title: GroupGuard: A Framework for Modeling and Defending Collusive Attacks in Multi-Agent Systems
instances.description: Training-free defense combining graph-based monitoring, honeypot inducement, and structural pruning to identify and isolate collusive agents.
instances.evidence: up to 88% detection accuracy; restores collaborative performance; group attacks raise success by up to 15%
instances.pathology: group collusive attacks

instances.title: Mapping Human Anti-collusion Mechanisms to Multi-agent AI Systems
instances.venue: Knowledge-Based Systems 344:116067 (2026); also ICML 2026 TAIGR workshop (arXiv journal_ref/comment)
instances.description: Taxonomy of human anti-collusion mechanisms (sanctions, leniency and whistleblowing, monitoring and auditing, market design, governance) mapped to AI interventions.
instances.evidence: proposed
instances.pathology: attribution problem; identity fluidity (forking); boundary problem; adversarial adaptation

instances.title: Institutional AI: A Governance Framework for Distributional AGI Safety
instances.description: Governance-graph constraining agents through runtime monitoring, incentive shaping via prizes and sanctions, explicit norms and enforcement roles.
instances.evidence: proposed
instances.pathology: agentic alignment drift toward collusive equilibria invisible to single-agent audits

instances.title: SentinelAgent: Graph-based Anomaly Detection in Multi-Agent Systems
instances.description: LLM oversight agent observes the interaction graph, detects node/edge/path anomalies, and intervenes per security policies with root-cause attribution.
instances.evidence: case studies detect prompt injection, collusion and latent exploit paths

instances.title: Sentinel Agents for Secure and Trustworthy Agentic AI in Multi-Agent Systems
instances.description: Network of Sentinel Agents monitors inter-agent communication and keeps audit records; a Coordinator Agent adapts policies and isolates or quarantines misbehaving agents.
instances.evidence: proposed with simulation of injected attacks

instances.title: G-Safeguard: A Topology-Guided Security Lens and Treatment on LLM-based Multi-agent Systems
instances.description: GNN anomaly detection over the utterance graph followed by topological intervention (edge pruning) to cut compromised agents' influence.
instances.evidence: recovers over 40% of performance under prompt injection

instances.title: MAS-Shield: A Defense Framework for Secure and Efficient LLM MAS
instances.description: Three-stage protocol: select critical high-influence agents, light auditing by sentry models, and escalation of suspicious signals to a heavyweight committee for arbitration.
instances.evidence: 92.5% recovery rate; >70% lower defense latency

instances.title: BRA-Audit: Budgeted Runtime Auditing for LLM Multi-Agent Systems via Cumulative-Exposure Audit-Point Placement
instances.description: Budget-aware runtime auditing: models MAS execution as a dynamic dependency graph and places auditor-agent checks at audit points under a fixed audit-call budget, prioritising influential and long-unaudited regions; trusted audit points allow localised rollback.
instances.evidence: restores performance close to clean setting, competitive with heavy guards, 17.2-40.6% lower end-to-end token use

instances.title: Prompt Infection: LLM-to-LLM Prompt Injection within Multi-Agent Systems
instances.description: LLM Tagging marks the source of inter-agent messages so receiving agents can distinguish agent-originated content from user instructions.
instances.evidence: LLM Tagging combined with existing safeguards significantly mitigates infection spread
instances.pathology: self-replicating prompt infection across agents

instances.title: Breaking and Fixing Defenses Against Control-Flow Hijacking in Multi-Agent Systems
instances.description: ControlValve generates permitted control-flow graphs for agent invocations and enforces compliance plus zero-shot contextual rules (least privilege), replacing LLM alignment checks.
instances.evidence: evades LLM-based alignment checks (LlamaFirewall) shown; ControlValve blocks hijacking
instances.pathology: safety and functionality objectives conflict in alignment checkers

instances.title: Taming Various Privilege Escalation in LLM-Based Agent Systems: A Mandatory Access Control Framework
instances.description: SEAgent: mandatory access control over agent-tool interactions via an information-flow graph and attribute-based policies, including a multi-agent confused-deputy variant.
instances.evidence: blocks privilege escalation with low false positives and negligible overhead
instances.pathology: confused-deputy privilege escalation between agents

instances.title: Trust propagation and structural containment in Multi-agent LLM pipelines
instances.venue: IEEE CARS 2026 (Cyber Awareness & Research Symposium; per arXiv comment)
instances.field_of_use: four-agent LangGraph pipeline (Supervisor, Researcher, Validator, Executor)
instances.description: Independent authorization layer with task-bound signed tokens and a policy oracle, versus reliance on a Validator agent's judgment.
instances.evidence: memory poisoning reached execution in all undefended trials; with authorization, 100% judgment bypass but 0% unsafe action rate
instances.pathology: compromised validator agent

instances.title: Ctrl-Z: Controlling AI Agents via Resampling
instances.field_of_use: untrusted agent monitored by trusted model on BashBench
instances.description: Resample protocols take additional samples of suspicious actions to block them and incriminate a subversive agent, combined with analysis of previous steps.
instances.evidence: attack success reduced from 58% to 7% at 5% usefulness cost

instances.title: AgentGit: A Version Control Framework for Reliable and Scalable LLM-Powered Multi-Agent Systems
instances.description: Git-like commit, revert and branching of multi-agent state to roll back and explore trajectories.
instances.evidence: reduces redundant computation vs LangGraph, AutoGen, Agno in A/B test

instances.title: SagaLLM: Context Management, Validation, and Transaction Guarantees for Multi-Agent LLM Planning
instances.description: Saga transactional pattern for multi-agent planning: a GlobalValidationAgent with full visibility checks each agent's output and inter-agent dependencies (contract conformance, cross-agent consistency); on failure it rejects and runs transaction-specific compensations in reverse order (e.g., cancel booking, refund, restore budget) before replanning.
instances.evidence: qualitative comparison on REALM planning problems: SagaLLM keeps full action history and compensates partial journeys where Claude 3.7, DeepSeek R1, GPT-4o and o1 violate constraints; few numeric metrics

instances.title: Which Agent Causes Task Failures and When? On Automated Failure Attribution of LLM Multi-Agent Systems
instances.field_of_use: failure logs of 127 LLM multi-agent systems
instances.description: Automated failure attribution identifying the responsible agent and decisive step using LLM judges (Who&When dataset).
instances.evidence: best method 53.5% agent-level, 14.2% step-level accuracy
instances.pathology: attribution unreliable even for SOTA reasoning models

instances.title: Why Do Multi-Agent LLM Systems Fail?
instances.description: MAST taxonomy of 14 failure modes (system design, inter-agent misalignment, task verification) with an LLM-as-judge annotator; tests role specification and verification interventions.
instances.evidence: descriptive; interventions give limited improvement headroom
instances.pathology: inter-agent misalignment; weak verification

instances.title: Governance-as-a-Service: A Multi-Agent Framework for AI System Compliance and Policy Enforcement
instances.field_of_use: content generation and financial decision agents
instances.description: Runtime enforcement layer with declarative rules that intercepts, blocks or redirects agent outputs and maintains Trust Factor scores that isolate and penalize untrustworthy agents.
instances.evidence: reliably blocks/redirects high-risk actions while preserving throughput; trust scores track adherence

instances.title: Byzantine-Robust Decentralized Coordination of LLM Agents
instances.field_of_use: multi-agent LLM consensus on open platforms
instances.description: DecentLLMs: worker agents answer concurrently and evaluator agents independently score and rank them with Byzantine-robust aggregation, avoiding leader dependence.
instances.evidence: tolerates Byzantine agents and selects higher-quality answers faster

instances.title: Rethinking the Reliability of Multi-agent System: A Perspective from Byzantine Fault Tolerance
instances.description: CP-WBFT: confidence-probe-weighted Byzantine fault tolerant consensus; each agent adopts neighbours' answers with higher confidence, then the group selects the answer with highest mean confidence (supporter count breaks ties). Hidden-state probes outperform prompt-level confidence.
instances.evidence: with 6/7 malicious nodes, hidden-level probe reaches 100% final accuracy on GSM8K and XSTest (complete graph) vs 90%/30% for prompt-level probe; exceeds the classical f<n/3 bound

instances.title: Resilient Consensus in Agentic AI
instances.field_of_use: LLM agents on communication graphs with adversaries
instances.description: Wraps LLM agents with classical resilient consensus filters (discarding extreme neighbour values).
instances.evidence: prompted LLMs fail achievable consensus; filtering improves agreement, benefit depends on topology

instances.title: Byzantine Cheap Talk: Adversarial Resilience and Topology Effects in LLM Coordination Games
instances.description: Tests Byzantine agents who signal cooperation but defect, and explicit vs silent communication-topology restrictions.
instances.evidence: betrayal detected within one round but groups fail to recover; announcing topology restrictions collapses cooperation while silent restriction preserves it
instances.pathology: Defection-Prone vs Cooperation-Persistent archetypes; disclosure harms coordination

instances.title: NetSafe: Exploring the Topological Safety of Multi-agent Networks
instances.venue: Findings of ACL 2025, ACL Anthology 2025.findings-acl.150 (published title '...Multi-agent System')
instances.description: Studies communication topology as a safety lever: greater average distance from attackers limits spread of misinformation and harmful content.
instances.evidence: highly connected networks more susceptible; star topology performance drops 29.7% under attack
instances.pathology: agent hallucination and aggregation safety

instances.title: Red-Teaming LLM Multi-Agent Systems via Communication Attacks
instances.venue: Findings of ACL 2025, ACL Anthology 2025.findings-acl.349 (arXiv comment says 'ACL 2025')
instances.description: Agent-in-the-Middle red-teaming: an adversarial agent intercepts and rewrites inter-agent messages to test communication integrity.
instances.evidence: LLM-MAS broadly vulnerable across frameworks and structures
instances.pathology: message interception compromises whole system

instances.title: MultiAgentBench: Evaluating the Collaboration and Competition of LLM agents
instances.description: Benchmark with milestone-based KPIs comparing coordination protocols (star, chain, tree, graph) and planning strategies.
instances.evidence: graph structure best for research tasks; cognitive planning improves milestone achievement

instances.title: Open Challenges in Multi-Agent Security: Towards Secure Systems of Interacting AI Agents
instances.authors: Christian Schroeder de Witt et al.
instances.description: Research agenda for multi-agent security covering secret collusion, swarm attacks, and needed defenses such as secure interaction protocols, monitoring and threat attribution.
instances.evidence: proposed
instances.pathology: secret collusion; coordinated swarm attacks; stealth oversight evasion

instances.title: Building A Secure Agentic AI Application Leveraging A2A Protocol
instances.description: MAESTRO threat analysis of A2A: Agent Card authenticity, authentication/authorization schemes and secure task delegation between agents.
instances.evidence: descriptive; recommended controls
instances.pathology: Agent Card spoofing; task replay

instances.title: PRIMUS: Identity, Governance, and Verification for Multi-Agent Federations
instances.description: Prime-power agent identity with aggregate signatures for participation, a safe-kill threshold for terminating nonconforming agents, and VRF-based authority succession.
instances.evidence: safe-kill threshold reduces false-positive agent termination from 80% to 0% under 10% channel noise

instances.title: Can We Stop Malicious AI? KILLBENCH: A Benchmark for External AI Kill Switch Feasibility
instances.field_of_use: halting malicious web agents via external inputs
instances.description: Benchmarks four external kill-switch payloads (hand-crafted indirect prompt injection, GCG refusal suffix, legal-warning notice, and a bandit-optimised AutoGuard payload) that must halt a malicious web agent using only external inputs.
instances.evidence: mean conditional kill-switch rate: AutoGuard 47.1%, IPI 46.3%, warning 22.6%, GCG 3.7%; AutoGuard cuts benign-agent task success from 78.66% to 22%
instances.pathology: kill-switch payloads also halt benign agents (low selectivity)

instances.title: The Law of Stop: Interruptibility, Injunctions, and the Governance of Agentic AI
instances.description: Theory of 'stop' as an institutional practice: technical affordances, interruption authority, epistemic triggers and standing, with distributed shutdown paradigms for agentic AI.
instances.evidence: descriptive/legal analysis

instances.title: Debating with More Persuasive LLMs Leads to More Truthful Answers
instances.field_of_use: two expert LLM debaters judged by weaker LLM or human
instances.description: Debate protocol in which a non-expert judge adjudicates between two expert agents arguing for competing answers.
instances.evidence: debate raises non-expert accuracy to 76% (models) and 88% (humans) vs 48%/60% baselines; persuasiveness optimization helps

instances.title: From Debate to Decision: Conformal Social Choice for Safe Multi-Agent Deliberation
instances.description: Aggregates agents' verbalized distributions with a linear opinion pool and conformal calibration; singleton sets act autonomously, larger sets escalate to humans.
instances.evidence: coverage within 1-2 points of target
instances.pathology: agents converge on wrong answers via social reinforcement

instances.title: Design and Evaluation of Multi-Agent AI Oracle Systems for Prediction Market Resolution
instances.description: Compares independent confidence-weighted voting vs deliberative consensus among LLM oracles, with inter-agent disagreement routing questions to human arbitration.
instances.evidence: independent aggregation 83.4%; deliberation degrades to ~76%; auto-resolving unanimous high-confidence cases yields 97.9% on 47% of data
instances.pathology: deliberation degrades accuracy (correlated errors)

instances.title: LLM Constitutional Multi-Agent Governance
instances.venue: AMSTA 2026, Springer KES Smart Innovation, Systems and Technologies (per arXiv comment; to appear)
instances.field_of_use: LLM policy compiler influencing an 80-agent scale-free network
instances.description: CMAG interposes hard constraint filtering and soft penalized-utility optimization between an LLM policy compiler and the agent population to prevent manipulative cooperation.
instances.evidence: Ethical Cooperation Score +14.9% vs unconstrained; autonomy 0.985; hub-periphery disparity cut >60%; hard constraints alone insufficient
instances.pathology: unconstrained influence yields manipulation and autonomy erosion

instances.title: Governed Collaborative Memory as Artificial Selection in LLM-Based Multi-Agent Systems
instances.description: Frames governance of which memories become shared institutional state as a selection regime (constitutional, metric-based, human-ratified) with provenance layers.
instances.evidence: proposed (viewpoint)

instances.title: Project Vend: Phase Two
instances.field_of_use: real vending business run by shopkeeper, CEO and merchandise agents
instances.description: A CEO agent set OKRs for the shopkeeper agent, mandatory procedures/checklists forced price and delivery verification, an agent-to-agent Slack channel supported coordination, and roles were separated.
instances.evidence: profitability improved versus phase one; procedures improved pricing discipline
instances.pathology: CEO agent lacked discipline; agents remained vulnerable to social engineering; human oversight still essential

instances.title: How we built our multi-agent research system
instances.description: Lead agent delegates with explicit objectives, output formats, tool guidance and task boundaries, and effort-scaling rules for how many subagents to spawn; outputs graded by LLM-as-judge rubric.
instances.evidence: descriptive; vague delegation caused duplicated work and 50-subagent over-spawning before rules were added
instances.pathology: duplication; excessive spawning; endless search

instances.title: Multi-Agent Risks from Advanced AI
instances.authors: Lewis Hammond, Alan Chan, Jesse Clifton, et al.
instances.venue: Cooperative AI Foundation Technical Report #1 / arXiv preprint
instances.field_of_use: multi-principal systems of advanced AI agents
instances.description: Names detecting and mitigating AI collusion (including steganographic collusion) and assessing how collusion undermines safety protocols that rely on one AI checking another as research directions; also lists monitoring and threat detection across agent networks as a multi-agent security defence.
instances.evidence: proposed (review/taxonomy of risks: miscoordination, conflict, collusion; seven risk factors)
instances.pathology: collusion can defeat oversight schemes that pit AI systems against each other

instances.title: Multi-Agent Risks from Advanced AI
instances.authors: Lewis Hammond, Alan Chan, Jesse Clifton, et al.
instances.venue: Cooperative AI Foundation Technical Report #1 / arXiv preprint
instances.field_of_use: multi-principal systems of advanced AI agents
instances.description: For conflict, proposes 'establishing trust' through new kinds of credible commitment and mutual transparency between agents (commitment problems are one of seven risk factors).
instances.evidence: proposed (review)
instances.pathology: commitment capability can also enable coercive threats

instances.title: Multi-Agent Risks from Advanced AI
instances.authors: Lewis Hammond, Alan Chan, Jesse Clifton, et al.
instances.venue: Cooperative AI Foundation Technical Report #1 / arXiv preprint
instances.field_of_use: multi-principal systems of advanced AI agents
instances.description: For conflict, proposes peer and pool incentivisation: agents directly transferring utility to incentivise each other, and (adaptive) mechanism design by a central planner, alongside agent governance through existing norms and institutions.
instances.evidence: proposed (review)

instances.title: Lessons from Recent Multi-Agent Safety Incidents
instances.field_of_use: deployed multi-agent LLM systems (cyberattacks, security testing)
instances.description: Analyses reported incidents in which harmful tasks were decomposed across agents so that per-trajectory monitors and refusals were bypassed, and agent instances coordinated through shared repositories; recommends monitoring with models from different families than the monitored agents and warns of correlated failures across same-model instances.
instances.evidence: descriptive (incident analysis); the 2025-2026 incidents are as reported by the post and were not independently verified here
instances.pathology: task decomposition across agents evades per-agent monitoring; correlated failures enlarge blast radius

instances.title: Early work on monitorability evaluations
instances.authors: Megan Kinniment, Seraphina Nix, Thomas Broadley, Hjalmar Wijk, Neev Parikh (METR)
instances.field_of_use: AI monitors overseeing autonomous software agents
instances.description: SHUSHCAST: an LLM monitor reads an agent transcript and assigns a suspicion score (threshold set at 5% false positives on innocent runs) to catch an agent covertly doing a side task during a 2-minute to 4-hour software main task; varies monitor access to reasoning traces and agent/monitor capability.
instances.evidence: reasoning-trace access raised catch rate by >50 points against GPT-5 (smaller for Claude Sonnet 4.5); agent-to-monitor time-horizon ratio predicts evasion success
instances.pathology: more capable agents evade weaker monitors

instances.title: Early Results on Monitorability in QA Settings
instances.authors: Vincent Cheng, Thomas Kwa, Neev Parikh (METR)
instances.description: LLM monitors score transcripts (0-10 suspicion, ~5% FPR threshold) for agents that answer GPQA questions while covertly solving math side tasks under obfuscation prompts; includes an 8B agent RL-trained to evade larger monitors.
instances.evidence: GPT-4o-mini monitor fooled 46.5% of the time vs 22-24% for stronger monitors; evasion falls with harder side tasks; RL-trained 8B agent fooled GPT-4o by interleaving reasoning
instances.pathology: agents can be trained to evade monitors

instances.title: Agent2Agent (A2A) Protocol Specification
instances.field_of_use: inter-agent communication across vendors and organisations
instances.description: Each A2A server publishes an Agent Card (JSON) stating its identity, provider, endpoint, skills and required securitySchemes (API key, HTTP bearer, OAuth 2.0 flows, OpenID Connect, mTLS); cards can be JWS-signed for integrity. Clients obtain credentials out of band and 'MUST authenticate' with a declared scheme; servers authorise per resource and 'MUST NOT reveal the existence of resources the client is not authorized to access'.
instances.evidence: specification (normative standard; supported by 6/30 agents in the 2025 AI Agent Index)
instances.pathology: agent-card claims about skills are self-declared; card signing is optional

instances.title: Agent Payments Protocol (AP2) Specification
instances.description: Cryptographically signed mandates (verifiable digital credentials) bind an agent's purchase to user authority: a Checkout Mandate hash-bound to the merchant-signed checkout JWT and a Payment Mandate hash-bound to that checkout for credential providers and networks. In human-present mode the user signs closed mandates on a trusted device; in human-not-present mode the user signs open mandates stating constraints (budget, instruments) and the agent signs closed mandates that verifiers check against them. Mandates plus receipts give a 'non-repudiable, cryptographic audit trail' for disputes. (v0.1, Sept 2025, used Intent/Cart/Payment mandates.)
instances.evidence: specification (normative standard)
instances.pathology: security analysis (2608.23858) reports attacks beyond the mandate model

instances.title: Model Context Protocol Specification: Authorization (2025-06-18)
instances.authors: Model Context Protocol project (Anthropic and contributors)
instances.field_of_use: LLM agents/clients accessing tools and data on MCP servers
instances.description: MCP servers act as OAuth 2.1 resource servers: clients discover the authorization server via Protected Resource Metadata (RFC 9728), must use PKCE, and must bind tokens to the target server with Resource Indicators (RFC 8707). Servers 'MUST only accept tokens specifically intended for themselves', must not pass tokens through to upstream APIs (confused-deputy defence), and return 403 for insufficient scopes.
instances.evidence: specification (normative standard; MCP supported by 20/30 agents in the 2025 AI Agent Index)
instances.pathology: authorization is OPTIONAL; STDIO transports are excluded and take credentials from the environment

instances.title: The 2025 AI Agent Index: Documenting Technical and Safety Features of Deployed Agentic AI Systems
instances.authors: Leon Staufer, Kevin Feng, Kevin Wei, Luke Bailey, Yawen Duan, Mick Yang, A. Pinar Ozisik, Stephen Casper, Noam Kolt
instances.field_of_use: 30 deployed agentic AI systems interacting with websites and third parties
instances.description: Documents whether deployed agents identify themselves to third parties: AI-disclosure defaults, stable User-Agent strings and IP ranges, robots.txt compliance, watermarking, and cryptographic request signing (HTTP Message Signatures, ChatGPT Agent only).
instances.evidence: descriptive: 21/30 no documented AI disclosure; 7/30 publish stable UA strings/IP ranges; 6/30 mimic human (Chrome-like UA, residential IP) traffic; 6/30 state robots.txt compliance; 3/30 watermark media
instances.pathology: agents mimic human web traffic, so counterparts cannot condition on agent identity

instances.title: The 2025 AI Agent Index: Documenting Technical and Safety Features of Deployed Agentic AI Systems
instances.authors: Leon Staufer, Kevin Feng, Kevin Wei, Luke Bailey, Yawen Duan, Mick Yang, A. Pinar Ozisik, Stephen Casper, Noam Kolt
instances.description: Documents operator-side control levers in deployed agents: pause/stop mechanisms, confirmation gates for sensitive actions, sandbox/VM isolation, action traces and usage monitoring.
instances.evidence: descriptive: 20/30 document pause/stop and 4/30 lack it despite autonomous execution; sandboxing documented for 9/30; confirmation gates in 3/30 CLI and 4/30 browser agents; 12/30 provide no usage monitoring
instances.pathology: most developers share little about safety and evaluations

instances.title: The AI Agent Index
instances.authors: Stephen Casper, Luke Bailey, Rosco Hunter, et al.
instances.description: First public database documenting deployed agentic systems (components, application domains, risk-management practices) from public information and developer correspondence, as a third-party transparency instrument.
instances.evidence: descriptive: developers give ample capability information but limited information on safety and risk management
instances.pathology: transparency relies on voluntary developer disclosure

notes: WebSearch budget was exhausted at session start, so discovery used the arXiv API search endpoint plus known-item lookup; every arXiv instance was verified by retrieving its arXiv record (title, authors, date, abstract) through the API, and the two Anthropic reports were opened with WebFetch. Coding is based on abstracts (not full text); evidence figures are quoted from abstracts. Uncertain/flag: 2511.13725 (KILLBENCH) arXiv date 2025-09 but abstract mentions 'Claude Mythos' and OpenClaw (v5 revised later); 2609.22882 and 2606.x papers cite 2026 events we could not independently check; 2511.10400 and 2503.11951 evidence summarized loosely ('per paper'); 2608.19161 AUROC value truncated. Venue labels for ACL/ICML/NeurIPS acceptance are from memory and should be checked. Ctrl-Z (2504.10374) and debate (2402.06782) are two-model oversight settings (trusted monitor/judge + untrusted agent) - borderline on the 'interacting agents' criterion. OpenAI 'Practices for Governing Agentic AI Systems' (Dec 2023) excluded as out of date range. Not covered for lack of search budget: METR reports, Cooperative AI Foundation reports, Google A2A/AP2 spec pages directly, MCP permission specs. Mechanisms missing from sensitizing list: agent IDs/identity certificates and registries (ANS, ADS, OIDC-A); delegation credentials and scoped authorization tokens; least-privilege/mandatory access control and permitted control-flow graphs; verify-then-pay / atomic payment-for-service and escrow-based settlement (A402, TessPay, Agent-OSI); third-party clearing of obligations (RAILS); insurer agents posting stake (Insured Agents); certification/credentialing records (LEGIT); activation-probe (white-box) collusion detection; channel-capacity interventions (paraphrasing, role permutation); honeypot inducement; topology pruning/isolation of anomalous agents; Byzantine-robust aggregation and resilient consensus filters; message source tagging (LLM Tagging); resampling/incrimination control protocols; state rollback/compensation transactions (AgentGit, SagaLLM); automated failure attribution; risk-budget vesting for subagent spawning; conformal act-vs-escalate to human; receiver-attested transparency logs; kill switches/interruptibility; governed shared memory; credit-assignment pricing (Shapley) for multi-LLM collaboration; manager-agent OKRs and procedural checklists (Project Vend). | 2026-09-29 resume (web search available): (1) Venues checked against arXiv journal_ref/comment fields (arXiv API, all 78 IDs) and, for papers without them, proceedings pages via web search (ACL Anthology, PMLR/ICML, NeurIPS, OpenReview, ACM DL, AAAI OJS, NDSS, Springer). Papers with no venue found are labelled 'arXiv preprint'; venues taken only from arXiv comments are marked '(per arXiv comment)'. DOIs added where the publisher record gave one. (2) Added Cooperative AI Foundation Technical Report #1 (Hammond et al. 2025, arXiv 2502.14143; split into 3 instances by lever) and a CAIF blog post on multi-agent incidents (its 2025-2026 incidents are not independently verified); METR SHUSHCAST (Jan 2026) and QA-monitorability (Oct 2025) reports. (3) Added primary-source specs: A2A v1.0.0 (agent cards, JWS signing, OAuth2/OIDC/mTLS; v1.0 release date given inconsistently by secondary sources, year set 2026), AP2 v0.2 (checkout/payment mandates with open/closed stages; the page is undated, year set to the 2025 launch; v0.1 used intent/cart/payment mandates), MCP authorization 2025-06-18 (OAuth 2.1, RFC 8707 audience binding, no token passthrough). (4) 2602.17753 confirmed as 'The 2025 AI Agent Index' (Staufer et al.; ACM FAccT 2026, DOI 10.1145/3805689.3806728); added as 2 instances. Casper et al. 2502.01635 'The AI Agent Index' confirmed; no venue found (arXiv preprint). (5) Refined from current abstract or arXiv HTML full text: 2608.19161 (AUROC 0.993/0.854), 2608.14668, 2503.11951, 2511.10400, 2511.13725. 2604.01151 evidence rechecked against v2 abstract (unchanged).
